<explanation>

1. Project Type & Purpose  
   – ArchiveBox is an open-source, self-hosted web archiving tool.  
   – It combines a command-line interface (CLI), a Django-based web UI, a REST API, and background workers to ingest URLs, snapshot sites in multiple formats, and store both metadata (in SQLite) and content files on the filesystem.  

2. High-Level File Structure Analysis  
   • Top-level folders:  
     – archivebox/: core Django app (models, views, management commands, ASGI/WSGI)  
     – archivebox/api/: Django Ninja REST API endpoints  
     – archivebox/cli/: CLI commands wrapping the core library  
     – archivebox/core/: main Django project settings, URLs, middleware, templates  
     – archivebox/workers/: Huey task orchestration, actor processes, supervisord scripts  
     – archivebox/extractors/: modular scripts for snapshotting (wget, Chrome, yt-dl, git, etc.)  
     – archivebox/config/: load-and-persist configuration settings  
   • Supporting directories:  
     – bin/: build/test/release scripts, Docker entrypoint, linting  
     – etc/: sample config files, Docker Compose, Nginx, uWSGI  
     – docs/, .github/, website/: documentation and CI/CD pipelines  
     – tests/: pytest fixtures, unit/integration tests, mock servers  

3. README Insights  
   – Describes core components: CLI, web UI, Python API, REST API, scheduled imports.  
   – Highlights use of Django + Django-Ninja, Huey queue, SQLite + filesystem storage.  
   – Lists key external dependencies (Chrome, wget, yt-dl, git, singlefile, readability).  
   – Illustrates deployment options: Docker Compose, plain Docker, pip, package managers.  

4. Main Components for the Diagram  
   a. Clients & Inputs (left side):  
      • CLI (archivebox commands)  
      • Browser Extension / Bookmarklet feeds  
      • Scheduled import (cron / archivebox schedule)  
      • Python API calls  
      • REST API consumers  
   b. Web/API Layer (Django):  
      • Django Admin & custom views (archivebox/core/views)  
      • Django-Ninja REST API (archivebox/api/v1_*.py)  
      • URL routing (core/urls.py, api/urls.py)  
      • Configuration loader (archivebox/config)  
   c. Orchestration & Task Queue:  
      • Management commands & schedule runner  
      • Huey task queue (queue.sqlite3)  
      • Supervisord / Daphne / uWSGI coordinating web & worker processes  
   d. Workers & Extractors:  
      • archivebox/workers/worker.py executing tasks  
      • extractors submodules invoking external tools:  
        – wget cloning + WARC  
        – headless Chrome for PDF, screenshot, DOM dump, singlefile  
        – yt-dl for media  
        – git for repos  
        – post-processing (readability, metadata extraction)  
   e. Storage:  
      • SQLite database (index.sqlite3) for metadata (Snapshots, ArchiveResult logs)  
      • Filesystem archive/ folder for snapshot outputs (HTML, JSON, PDF, PNG, WARC, media/)  
      • Optional external backends (S3, B2, Google Drive via abx-pkg)  
      • Archive.org integration via curl API  
   f. External Services & Dependencies:  
      • Archive.org (optional remote backup)  
      • System tools: chrome/chromium, node/npm, wget, curl, yt-dl, git  

5. Relationships & Data Flow  
   1. Client adds URL via CLI / web UI / API → Django receives request.  
   2. Django creates Snapshot record in SQLite → enqueues snapshot job in Huey.  
   3. Worker process (Huey) fetches job → invokes one or more extractors in parallel.  
   4. Each extractor writes files to data/archive/TIMESTAMP/* and returns ArchiveResult.  
   5. Worker updates DB with ArchiveResult entries → Django admin/log reflects status.  
   6. Clients view snapshots via web UI or list via CLI (reading DB + serving static files).  
   7. Optional scheduled tasks re-enqueue jobs for feeds/bookmarks import.  

6. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   – Layered architecture separating presentation (CLI/UI/API), orchestration (Django core), and processing (workers).  
   – Asynchronous task queue (Huey) for long-running I/O-bound extraction jobs.  
   – Plugin-like extractors for modularity & extensibility.  
   – Filesystem as primary content storage; SQLite for light metadata.  
   – Containerized deployment with Docker Compose for reproducibility and isolation.  

7. Diagram Guidelines Tailored to ArchiveBox  
   • Use swimlanes or color bands for: Clients, Web/API Layer, Task Queue, Workers, Storage, External Tools/Services.  
   • Represent processes as boxes: “Django App Server”, “Huey Worker”, “Extractor: Wget”, etc.  
   • Draw arrows showing:  
     – Client → Django (HTTP / CLI call)  
     – Django → SQLite & filesystem (read/write)  
     – Django → Huey queue (enqueue)  
     – Worker → extractors → filesystem & DB  
     – Optional: Worker → Archive.org API  
   • Highlight technologies next to each component:  
     – Web/API: Django, Django-Ninja, Channels/Daphne, uWSGI  
     – Queue: Huey (SQLite)  
     – Workers: supervisord, Python  
     – Extractors: Chrome, wget, yt-dl, git, singlefile, readability  
   • Show deployment envelope: Docker Compose, containers for “archivebox” service, volume mounts for data/.  

8. Diagram Elements to Include  
   – Clear labels for each component and process.  
   – Directional arrows for data flows: URL ingestion, job dispatch, file writes, DB updates, user retrieval.  
   – Color coding or shapes:  
     • Blue for frontend/API (CLI, Browser, REST)  
     • Green for core backend (Django)  
     • Orange for task queue & workers  
     • Gray for extractors/external tools  
     • Brown for storage (SQLite, filesystem)  
     • Purple for external services (Archive.org, S3)  

9. Level of Detail  
   – Capture HTTP interactions, job queue pattern, worker–extractor orchestration, and storage strategy.  
   – Include background scheduler for feeds/bookmarks imports.  
   – Depict optional paths (scheduled vs one-shot vs browser extension).  
   – Do not overcrowd; group related extractors under a “Extractor Plugins” cluster.  
   – Annotate config sources (ArchiveBox.conf, env vars) influencing behavior.  

By following these guidelines, your system design diagram will accurately reflect ArchiveBox’s modular, asynchronous, and extensible architecture, making it clear how each component interacts to snapshot, store, and serve archived web content.  
</explanation>
